schedule: Adaptive selects the current highest-V move from the complete legal set, verifies it and supplies the existing coincident experimental feedback. Measure every legal candidate after every attempt. Keep all legal moves; never blacklist mistakes. Continue the fixed budget even after success to measure whether preference survives informative/no-pulse experiences. Unknown attempts produce no neural teaching event and consume the bounded attempt slot.
fixed: Replay the prior frozen informative schedule of eight reviewed experiences from naive gains, with a full-root sweep after each event. Same teaching budget, different sampling policy; not an exposure-matched control for the adaptive policy.
controls: Absent, shuffled and disabled replay EXACTLY the adaptive candidate/proof sequence, not their own preferred choices. Absent omits external pulses; shuffled phase-wide permutes known-event pulse flags with seed 13007, preserving count; disabled has informative pulses but no plasticity. If all flags coincide, shuffled is uninformative and must be reported as such, never as evidence of feedback specificity.
measurement: All-legal before/after-each-attempt score trajectories, verified preferred-move outcomes, correction/revival patterns, full-root repeat/reset/restoration, and final independent choice verification. Report fixed vs adaptive at equal attempts and actual known-event counts. No statistical generalization claim from one fixture.
acceptance: Fixture repair requires final adaptive unaided success, exact repeat/restoration and return to initial failure on reset. Descriptive informative specificity additionally requires nondegenerate shuffled flags, adaptive success and failure of all three sequence-matched controls. Keep failed gates. Broader biological/transfer/whole-model gates remain outside this fixture.
limitations: Same-position repair experiment with an engineered MBON readout, direct KC/PPL103 stimulation, coarse masks and unfitted local efficacy. No natural pathway, delayed credit through calculation, unfamiliar-family transfer or completed reasoning learner.
